articles.title: ‘My dog’s built her own fashion community’: how canine companions stole the fashion week spotlight
articles.summary: Our four-legged friends are turning heads from Louis Vuitton to Schiaparelli – but what does their presence in the most exclusive of spaces say about the industry’s changing attitudes? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: The front row at a fashion week show is a known hotspot for celebrities. During the most recent iteration that wrapped up on Tuesday, sightings included Heathcliff, AKA Jacob Elordi, high-fiving the Adolescence star Owen Cooper at Bottega Veneta; Rihanna arriving 63 minutes late to the Matières Fécales show; and Dua Lipa gossiping with Nicole Kidman and Pedro Pascal at Chanel. But peppered in among the Hollywood crowd was another type of guest going head-to-head for the photographers’ attention: dogs.

From a cavapoo at Louis Vuitton to a shih tzu at Schiaparelli, four-legged companions – rather than designer bags – sat on the laps of many showgoers. At the Balenciaga show, Brooklyn Beckham and Nicole Peltz sat next to Miranda Priestly – no, not Meryl Streep in her Devil Wears Prada character, but the brand’s creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli’s rescue dog. Tommy Hilfiger took his post-show bow with a fluffy samoyed – a look-a-like of Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s pup who stars with Kelce in a campaign for the brand. Elsewhere, a miniature schnauzer in goggles and a chihuahua wearing a puffer jacket took over the catwalk at Chopova Lowena.
points: Our four-legged friends are turning heads from Louis Vuitton to Schiaparelli – but what does their presence in the most exclusive of spaces say about the industry’s changing attitudes?

articles.title: Experience: I became the world’s oldest crowd surfer at 99
articles.summary: After retiring at 83, I had a new lease of life creating social media content with my grandson. Then I broke the crowd surfing world record. In 2013, aged 87, I was playing basketball with my grandson Ross in Ohio while he was home from college.
body: After doing lots of short videos, we decided to make a documentary about my life. As part of it, we compiled my bucket list. One of the things I wanted to do was break a world record. Ross and I spent months thinking of something that would be outrageous, but also fun and inclusive. We settled on me becoming the world’s oldest crowd surfer.

Ross knows the country singer Brantley Gilbert, and he was willing to help us at a show he was playing in Bellville, Texas. Originally, during the crowd surfing, I was going to be strapped to a board Ross had made to protect my back, but it was flexing too much, so he strapped me into a stretcher instead.

I was 99 years and 274 days old the day it happened. It was the first time I’d ever crowd surfed. To break the record, I had to stay up for at least 10 seconds. There were 20,000 people in the crowd – we planned for them to move me in a straight line from the back to the front. But 20 minutes before we were due to start, we saw that everyone in the main crowd was sitting in chairs with gaps between them. Ross started panicking. We used the mosh pit instead, and I travelled in a U-shape from stage right to stage left.

articles.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for toffee apple Basque cheesecake | The sweet spot
articles.summary: A crisp surface and creamy core are the traits of this cheesecake with no base, here topped with spiced and sliced apples and a sticky, caramel sauce. My go-to cheesecake these days is a burnt Basque.
body: I’ve given this an easy autumn spin with a generous topping of lightly spiced toffee apple slices.
Heat the oven to 240C (220C fan)/465F/gas 9. Scrunch up two large sheets of baking paper, then smooth them out into the corners of a deep 20cm cake tin.

Put the cream cheese, sugar and vanilla in a large bowl or stand mixer, and beat briefly until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, followed by the extra yolk, making sure you don’t beat at high speed to avoid incorporating too much air. Stir in the cream and salt.
Scoop about an eighth of the batter into a smaller bowl and sift the flour on top. Mix well to ensure there are no lumps, then scrape it back into the main mixture and stir well to combine.

articles.title: 24 Casual Wedding Guest Dresses for the Most Low-Key Fêtes
articles.summary: Wondering what constitutes a casual wedding guest dress? A bridal stylist weighs in—plus, the best pieces to wear from brands like Staud, Khaite, and Brandon Maxwell.
body: Decoding wedding dress codes can feel like a full-time job. As a bridal stylist, I field questions about them regularly—and of all the directives printed on wedding invitations, “casual” may be the most deceptively simple. It rarely means what it does on a Saturday spent out and about, and the line between relaxed and underdressed is thinner than many guests expect.

Casual attire usually signals a daytime or more laid-back setting, such as a backyard garden party, seaside vows, or an intimate vineyard lunch. That isn’t license to wear whatever you want, though. Denim, shorts, athleisure, head-to-toe sequins, formal gowns, and anything that reads like beachwear are not right here. Sneakers are also generally off-limits, as are white, ivory, and anything that could be mistaken for bridal (a rule at every wedding, of course, but worth repeating).
Here, browse 24 dresses that strike the right balance, from party-ready minis to LBDs.
points: Wondering what constitutes a casual wedding guest dress?

articles.title: Greta Van Fleet Is Still Burning Bright
articles.summary: Josh Kiszka explains to Vogue why, after a three-year break, Greta Van Fleet is back and more plugged in than ever.
body: It’s early afternoon in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, and the boys who make up the rock band Greta Van Fleet—lead singer Josh Kiszka; his twin, guitarist Jake; their younger bassist brother Sam; and drummer Danny Wagner—have convened in a studio as they prepare to sign heaping piles of their fourth studio album, Palace for the People. (It’s out today.) Contemplating the task ahead of them, Josh can’t help but reminisce about the Michigan-born band’s first time in the city, just as they were breaking into the mainstream. “It was just total culture shock,” he tells Vogue. “Back then, I couldn’t be here for more than a week because it was just too overstimulating.”

Just under a decade later, they’re plenty used to the hustle and bustle now. Propelled by lyrics rich with emotion, Josh’s trademark falsetto, and a general fondness for theatricality, Greta Van Fleet has established itself as a keeper of rock’s sacred flame, racking up four Grammy nominations and one win, for best rock album in 2019.
Vogue: You’ve managed to stand the test of time for the better part of a decade. What do you attribute that to?
points: Josh Kiszka explains to Vogue why, after a three-year break, Greta Van Fleet is back and more plugged in than ever.

articles.title: The Scoop With Guess’s Nicolai Marciano: On the Brand’s Latest Campaign and New Ambassador
articles.summary: This week’s guest is Guess Inc.’s chief new business development officer, Nicolai Marciano. Nicolai has officially worked for the company for 13 years, but as the son of co-founder Paul Marciano, that really means he started the job when he was zero.
body: Welcome to The Scoop, a weekly email series in which I ask fashion insiders to give me a piece of news they haven’t shared elsewhere.

It was the first time Guess worked together with what he calls “an opinion leader” to create products that celebrated the archive and a campaign focused on storytelling. All things Nicolai stands for, and that are at the core of the new Guess campaign, which he just gave me the scoop on.

Becky G will be the new ambassador for Guess’s B Jean. The campaign is coming out on October 13, and we’re excited because it’s a different format for us. Guess has been known for traditional film photography, still images, often black and white... This campaign is very looped into music, movement, and film, which feels in line with the spirit of Guess, but also organic for someone like Becky.

articles.title: 28 Best Hotels in Bali, From Oceanview Villas to Jungle-Immersed Escapes
articles.summary: Epic bathtubs, frangipani-laden landscaping, and some of the warmest hospitality anywhere await.
body: There’s quite simply no place like Bali. The jewel of Indonesia’s immense archipelago is rich—in enthralling and elaborate, highly embellished cultural customs; in hyperlocal culinary traditions and memorable flavors, natural wonders not to mention world-class waves, indelible art and design, encyclopedic wellness practices. And that’s just a bit of what the island offers. It’s captivated travelers for a century, and a stream of expats continues to flow to Bali—myself included—to make it their paradisiacal home away from home, while scores of the millions of holiday visitors wish they could make it so.

With each hospitality opening, whether an emerald-toned resort in the jungle or a boutique bolthole perched above a flawless beach, the challenge of choosing the perfect place to stay grows greater. I can hardly name a favorite after years of exploring, living and loving the people and practices that make it so singular. Still, I’ve narrowed down, from thousands, the 28 best hotels in Bali to book now, including the pioneering legends, innovating icons and newcomers doing things their own way.
